images.subparts: One shared Cartesian frame; no panels.
objectsAndLabels: Vertical amplitude axis with upward arrow; printed amplitude symbol X with Cyrillic descriptive subscript м.
Horizontal angular-frequency axis with rightward arrow and omega at the right.

Single thick solid curve starts on the vertical axis at positive amplitude, rises gradually, reaches one rounded high narrow peak, falls steeply then more gradually to a finite positive right endpoint.
A dashed vertical guide extends from the frequency axis to approximately the curve peak and is labelled omega_0 beneath the frequency axis.
relationships: The axes share an origin and are perpendicular.
The source guide treats the narrow peak as approximately aligned with omega_0.
The finite right curve endpoint is above the horizontal axis and left of its arrowhead.
There are no numeric ticks, measured units, grid, measured query coordinates, stated maximum value, apparatus, or answer.
modernRegularization: Straight perpendicular axes, smooth finite curve and readable English amplitude/frequency labels replace scanned stroke irregularities.

Keep omega_0 as the undamped natural-frequency guide; place the amplitude peak slightly left of it, explicitly implementing the retained source footnote and current text for nonzero weak linear damping.
All coordinates and curve control points are drawing coordinates, not measured physical data. No added visible numeric values.

images.subparts: One shared Cartesian frame for all three curves; no panels.
objectsAndLabels: Vertical amplitude axis with upward arrow and X with Cyrillic descriptive subscript м.
Horizontal angular-frequency axis with rightward arrow, omega at the right and 0 below its intersection with the amplitude axis.
Dashed vertical guide labelled omega_0, ending near the tallest peak.
Three distinct solid amplitude curves begin together at a positive intercept on the vertical axis.
Curve 1 is tallest and sharpest; curve 2 is intermediate; curve 3 is lowest and broadest.
The tallest and middle peaks are approximately aligned with the guide; the broad lowest peak is visibly somewhat left of the guide. No exact peak frequencies are printed.
Three labels 1, 2, 3 on the right have left/down-pointing leader arrows to the right slopes of their corresponding curves.
The three right tails remain distinct and end above the horizontal axis, ordered 1 above 2 above 3. Stroke interruptions at crowded leader locations are not a dashed-curve convention.
relationships: All curves use the same axes and frequency guide.
The text assigns 1 to least friction, 3 to greatest and the middle curve to intermediate friction, at equal drive amplitudes.
The three curve peaks decrease in height and broaden from 1 to 3.
All three finite endpoints are to the left of the horizontal-axis arrowhead and above its baseline.
No numeric ticks, measured units, grid, queried coordinates, exact peak values, apparatus, or answer is supplied.
modernRegularization: Keep three solid paths and three correctly attached arrow leaders in one frame.
Use only semantic vector color roles and readable English labels.

Make the amplitude peaks lie slightly below the undamped natural frequency in the frequency direction, with increasing shift as linear damping grows; this is model regularization justified by the source footnote/current text, not a recovered numerical reading.
Use a common positive left endpoint and distinct positive ordered right endpoints; coordinates carry no physical measurements.
